sources.text:
- Published
England striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is set to sign a new contract at Leeds United.
The 29-year-old, who has scored 20 goals in 49 appearances for the Whites since arriving on a free from Everton, currently has a deal until 2028 at Elland Road.
The news will come as a blow to Manchester United, who are looking at bringing in a forward in January after Benjamin Sesko was ruled out for an extended period as he tries to recover from a shin injury.
The Old Trafford side had been linked with Calvert-Lewin and a potential transfer in the January window.
He was recalled to the England squad by Thomas Tuchel in March and, though he missed out on selection for the World Cup, was picked for the most recent Nations League matches, winning his 14th cap on 6 October in the 3-0 victory over the Czech Republic.

sources.text:
If you’ve been waiting for a good deal on Google’s latest smartwatch before you commit, you're in luck. The Google Pixel Watch 5 (the 41-mm model with Wi-Fi) is currently $300, down from $400, marking its lowest price yet. (The larger 45-mm model is also discounted, from $430 to $330.)
This early Black Friday sale means you don’t have to wait until the late-November holiday to score the worthwhile discount—and we recommend you don't. Amazon, Best Buy, and the Google Store are all offering the 25 percent off deal, but I don't know for how much longer. In other words, now is a great time to score this smartwatch for less.
A Record-Low Price
The Pixel Watch 5 is one of the best smartwatches available for Android users. It’s a refinement of an already brilliant wearable, with double the RAM and storage, plus an upgraded Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 processor that makes this edition 20 percent faster than its predecessor. The domed display is gorgeous, comfortable, and easy to read during workouts, and it provides meaningful upgrades for health and fitness tracking.
Beyond being able to track weights and reps, the new Strength Training experience includes a workout builder, audio cues, and rest times. You can build a custom routine in the Google Health app and have the watch guide you through each exercise, and incorporate Gemini AI by asking it to generate a workout based on a photo of your gym equipment. Speaking of Gemini, the Pixel Watch 5 supports certain offline tasks, such as starting a workout, which is nice if you like to leave your watch at home while you exercise.
Google’s new Health Guardian tools include features for monitoring insulin resistance trends, blood pressure trends, breathing emergencies (available only in select countries), and sleep breathing quality. The watch also retains useful features like ECG, skin temperature tracking, and loss-of-pulse detection. It comes with upgraded sleep tracking, too, with Google claiming 15 percent greater accuracy than the Pixel Watch 4.
Google estimates up to 40 hours of battery life, but mine only got to around 36 hours in testing before conking out. Fast charging is the real standout, though; just 15 minutes on the charger delivers up to 15 hours of use. If you’re like me and only remember to charge your watch 20 minutes before leaving the house, this is a lifesaver.
At its original $400 price, the Pixel Watch 5 is a pricey recommendation, especially since many of its software upgrades will also make their way to the previous generation. But at $300, it’s cheaper than the latest Apple Watch Series 12 and other high-end smartwatches. This is the lowest price I’ve seen for the Pixel Watch 5, so if you’ve been eyeing it, there’s little reason to wait for Black Friday.

sources.title: Spurs' Maddison fit to face Palace - De Zerbi
sources.text:
- Published
Tottenham midfielder James Maddison is available to face Crystal Palace on Saturday despite an injury scare last week, manager Roberto De Zerbi says.
The 29-year-old England international limped off in the 51st minute of Spurs' 2-0 victory at Chelsea.
It sparked worries about Maddison's fitness, after he missed the majority of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.
Maddison then fractured his shoulder in Tottenham's opening weekend defeat at Brentford this season, before returning to the starting line-up earlier this month when he scored a spectacular goal in a 3-1 win against Coventry.
When asked about Maddison's condition, De Zerbi said he will be "available" for the visit of Palace.
"This week he didn't work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us," said De Zerbi.
"For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks - he is working very hard and consistently.
"So, I think it's not a problem if he loses two days [training], but then we have to analyse if we take the risk or not."
Tottenham have beaten Coventry and Chelsea since Maddison's return to the starting line-up, with the club 14th in the Premier League after climbing out of the relegation zone.
Maddison joined Tottenham from Leicester City in 2023 on a five-year contract in a deal worth £40m.
He's scored 17 goals and provided 21 assists in 85 appearances for the north London club.

sources.title: Villa to sue Carragher over 'unacceptable insults'
sources.text:
- Published
Aston Villa say they will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher over what the club branded as "unacceptable insults".
Posting on their social media on Friday, Villa released a statement signed by their chairman Nassef Sawiris accusing Carragher of insulting the Premier League side and its fans.
It added the club would "not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football".
Speaking on the Stick to Football podcast, Carragher attracted criticism from Villa fans by suggesting their manager Unai Emery would be interested in becoming Manchester United's head coach.
Michael Carrick's position at United is hanging in the balance after a dismal start to the campaign and Carragher said "Aston Villa will never be Manchester United".
"Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again," Carragher said.
"There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.
"So Real Madrid will take Manchester United's best player, they did it with [Cristiano] Ronaldo.
"And there will be teams below Aston Villa, and they'll take their players or manager, so shut the [expletive] up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United."
Carragher, a football pundit for works for Sky Sports and American broadcaster CBS, has already commented on the backlash he received after he told the fans to shut up.
"It was a joke after the stick Villa fans have given me over saying Emery may fancy joining Man Utd," Carragher said on social media.
"I hope these clown clips show me praising Emery/Villa like I have done for years & saying how pleased I was you won [the 2026 Europa League] in Istanbul."
On the Overlap Daily, Carragher went into more detail.
"I just think Unai Emery is the best manager in the league and if you're Man Utd you're thinking 'what's the best we can get?'. I'm not saying he'll go - I'm just saying if it was me I'd ask the question," said Carragher.
"Certain managers are good at certain clubs and that's Emery. He reminds me of Rafa [Benitez]. I think your own ego if someone said 'that's your level' would say 'no I'm not'. That was my point.
"It's grew arms and legs. I ended up telling them to [expletive] which maybe I shouldn't have done but it was all in jest because they've been all over my social timeline. I was saying [expletive] off my socials."

sources.title: Verbruggen spreads belief as impressive Brighton beat Man City
sources.text:
- Published
When the full-time whistle sounded at Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon, there was a striking contrast in the emotions of the players from Manchester City and Brighton.
Three days after losing to City on penalties in the Carabao Cup fourth round, the Seagulls achieved a 1-0 victory in the Premier League rematch, bouncing back to underline why they must be taken seriously towards the top of the table this season.
It was no coincidence that most of the Brighton players made a beeline for the outstanding Bart Verbruggen.
The Netherlands goalkeeper made seven saves during a phenomenal afternoon's work to help Brighton not only secure three points but also earn a fifth clean sheet in six Premier League matches.
Verbruggen's finest moment came during the second half when he produced a sprawling save down to his right to keep out a fierce effort from Matheus Nunes and deny City an equaliser.
Head coach Fabian Hurzeler commended Verbruggen's display for "spreading belief" as Brighton became the first visiting side to keep a Premier League clean sheet at the Etihad since Tottenham in August 2025.
"It's important to have this mindset and to spread it around the environment we work in, and belief is key to winning these types of games," said Hurzeler.
"Coming here to City, against one of the best teams in the league, is always special. You have to be brilliant at the basics and everyone was contributing.
"From Tuesday, when we travelled [to Manchester], we wanted to have a good four days, enjoy it and finish strong. Everyone can enjoy this win today."
'We celebrate and go again'
There could have very easily been a different outcome.
This was an afternoon when Manchester City accumulated an xG of 1.92, compared to 1.00 for Brighton, so there was no shortage of chances for the hosts.
Home head coach Enzo Maresca will be all too aware that City will have to rediscover their finishing touch - and quickly - if they are to mark his debut campaign in charge with a first Premier League title since 2024.
Manchester City had 21 shots on target without scoring, their highest number without doing so in the Premier League since November 2024, when they managed 24 in a game and drew a blank.
When Maresca sits down to pick apart his side's shortcomings, he will look rueful at chances from Iliman Ndiaye, Abdukodir Khusanov and Nunes in particular.
But to say Brighton's victory only came because of an off performance from City would be an extreme injustice to Hurzeler's side, who are quickly becoming one of the most well-rounded in the Premier League.
In addition to being the division's highest scorers - having found the back of the net 24 times in nine matches this season - Brighton have also kept the most clean sheets (six).
Only Premier League champions Arsenal - who have played one game less and travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday - have conceded fewer goals than Brighton's seven. Arsenal have shipped five, going into the Liverpool game.
One of the main reasons behind Brighton's solid rearguard has been the signing of Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham Hotspur.
The 19-year-old has been a transformative figure since arriving at Amex Stadium for a club record fee in July, starting all nine Premier League matches.
The Croatian has formed a rock-solid partnership with fellow centre-back Lewis Dunk and built an understanding with goalkeeper Verbruggen, all of whom played the full 90 minutes at the Etihad.
"It was a good game from all of us," said Verbruggen. "I'm happy to help the team and make some important saves, but I wasn't the only one.
"I think there were four or five shots blocked in an amazing way as well. It was a joint effort from everyone. We celebrate and go again."
Brighton not getting carried away by title talk
They couldn't, could they?
That's the question football supporters up and down the country are asking themselves as Brighton continue to soar up the Premier League table.
The Seagulls sit third, just two points behind Arsenal and Manchester City, and are making a strong case to become the Premier League's most unlikely title challengers since Leicester City, priced at 5,000-1 by bookmakers, achieved the unthinkable in May 2016.
Brighton's steady rise since returning to the top flight in 2017 means any potential title triumph would come as less of a shock than the feat of Claudio Ranieri's fantastic Foxes.
Saturday's victory over Manchester City followed a 3-0 win against Arsenal in September.
These are results that will only strengthen the belief that something special - whether a first Premier League title or Champions League qualification - could be achieved this season.

clusters.title_hint: SpaceX loses bid to toss NAACP lawsuit over Memphis data center air pollution

sources.title: SpaceX loses bid to toss NAACP lawsuit over Memphis data center air pollution
sources.text: The Colossus data centers and a power plant that SpaceXAI is also building in Southaven, Mississippi, have faced community backlash for years.

sources.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
sources.text:
A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis.
Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act.
xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue.
“Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision.
Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.”
TechCrunch has reached out to SpaceX for comment.
In a statement, the NAACP’s director of environmental and climate justice Abre’ Connor described this as “another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable.” (A similar motion to dismiss from the Department of Justice was denied earlier this month)
“The courts have repeatedly rejected attempts by xAI and the DOJ to dismiss the NAACP’s Clean Air Act case, affirming our right to pursue justice for communities impacted by pollution,” Connor said. “Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits.”
The NAACP lawsuit is moving forward as public opinion seems to have turned sharply against data centers, with New York recently passing a moratorium on new data centers and other state and local governments considering similar measures.
The backlash also prompted Amazon and Microsoft to promise to stop using NDAs in their dealings with government agencies, and it could be a significant factor in the imminent U.S. midterm elections.

sources.text:

clusters.title_hint: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away

sources.title: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away
sources.text:
2 min read
In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Using six gravity assists between them, this Grand Tour gave us up-close views of the gas and ice giants, including several moons. By the 1980s, the two probes went their separate ways at Saturn. As Voyager 2 continued toward Uranus and Neptune, Voyager 1 grabbed one more portrait of the solar system (excluding Mercury and Mars), including a final image of the pale blue dot we call home.
“Hello from the children of planet Earth.”
Every good road trip needs some music to match. In this case, each craft carries the Golden Record, a 12-inch phonograph record with spoken greetings in 55 languages, 27 musical tracks, 116 images, and other sounds from Earth. Each record is protected by an outer cover featuring etchings showing our Sun’s location relative to 14 pulsars, along with instructions on how to play it. The design used various metals to protect the information encoded from space radiation: the record used copper and gold plating, and the cover used aluminum. The cover was electroplated with an ultra-pure sample of the isotope uranium-238. Uranium-238 has a half-life of 4.468 billion years.
Did you know that a light-minute is a measure of distance, not time? In August 2012 and November 2018, Voyager 1 and 2 crossed the heliopause, the boundary where the Sun’s solar wind meets the interstellar medium. Using NASA’s Deep Space Network, Earth communicates with both spacecraft and tracks each on its journey. At the time of this article, the Canberra antenna tracked Voyager 1 at 25.80 billion km, or just over 16 billion miles.
On November 18, 2026, 49 years after its launch, Voyager 1 will cross the one-light-day mark, 16.1 billion miles from the Sun. You may have heard the term light-year in your favorite sci-fi movie or show, or when stargazing and referring to an object outside of our solar system. This video best demonstrates the different distances between the inner solar system, outer solar system, and beyond, using light measurements. Additionally, track each Voyager spacecraft here.
You can get a real understanding of what a gravity assist might be like with our Gravity Assist activity and learn what it’s like to measure a “light minute” with our Measuring a Kid Minute activity guide!

clusters.title_hint: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals

sources.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
sources.text:
While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.
“As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.”
Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI, a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther, a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS.
Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument.
Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours.
The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula.
Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon.
Learn more about NVIDIA AI for science.

Explanation:What spooky planet is this? Planet Earth on a dark and stormy night, of course. The ghostly scene was photographed at Hverir, a geothermally active area found along northeastern Iceland’s volcanic landscape. Triggered by solar activity, geomagnetic storms have unleashed energetic particles trapped in Earth’s magnetic field. Penetrating the planet’s upper atmosphere at high latitudes, the particles create auroral displays in the starry night sky. Ghostly towers of steam and gas are venting from local fumaroles to dance against the eerie, greenish northern lights. For now, auroral activity on planet Earth remains in a high state as the Sun is only in early phases of decline from the peak of its solar activity cycle. The brief ceremony introducing the new Macbook Pro this week was as low-key as the presenter, Apple’s new CEO John Ternus. He stepped onto the low stage at a Los Angeles event space with zero fanfare, said hi, and queued up a video showing the first touchscreen Mac. Then he released the modest crowd of journalists and creators to get hands-on with the new laptop and roam between eye-popping demos of music producers, filmmakers, photographers, and fashion designers using the laptop. Ternus, who at 51 is on the younger side of Apple’s top management, has been CEO for less than two months. But this launch and a series of other recent announcements have made one thing clear. With this new guy—if a 25-year Apple veteran could be considered new—it’s all about the products. Perhaps fittingly, the biggest noise of the presentation came when Ternus revealed that the new device restores the illumination to the Apple logo. Maybe that’s a symbol that in the age of AI, Apple is beaming out the message that hardware still rules.
A few minutes after the presentation, I sat down with Ternus, for the second time in two days. Steve Jobs used to grant me an audience after his famous keynotes, too. Ternus isn’t Jobs, of course, nor is he supposed to be. But who is he?
I first met Ternus in 2015, when I spent a day with him at Apple’s Input Design Lab, a testing facility in Cupertino. He’d risen to VP for Mac, iPad, Ecosystem, and Audio Engineering, and he struck me as affable and knowledgeable. (He spent four years right out of college at a virtual reality company, but he’s been at Apple ever since.) The peg to my story at the time was how this unknown manager conducted a Javert-like investigation to fix the weird sound a redesigned mouse made when sliding on a table.
That attention to detail was a legacy of Jobs’ perfectionism, which Tim Cook sustained as the next CEO. In the decade when Ternus overlapped with Jobs, he says he had only “a handful of interactions” with the founder. “But I've always felt like sort of a student of Steve's teachings,” Ternus said. “And then being able to work very closely with Tim, I’ve been very lucky.”
Ternus has so far been defined by his product prowess. “John innately has a great sense for great products, and that’s what Apple is,” says Greg Joswiak, Apple’s SVP of worldwide marketing and a 40-year company veteran. “You can’t teach that.” In one sense Ternus’ ascension is similar to that of Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, another lifer promoted to the top post. But Nadella was called upon to fix a broken organization, while Apple has been on a multi-decade run. Ternus is explicit that he will be an engine of continuity. That word is key to his selection, and above all explains why Tim Cook and the rest of Apple’s board was so comfortable with the choice.
The extent to which Ternus is a deep Apple insider became clear when I probed him on his views on being a corporate leader. I asked him which non-Apple CEOs he admires, and he was stumped. “I haven't really thought about that,” he said. I asked whether any business books had an impact on him. “Not really,” he said. “Of course I’ve read books, but there's so much to be learned from the people I get to work with.” Indeed, every time I tried to pin down Ternus on what mark he wants to make at Apple, he deflected the question and told me how he will continue Apple’s commitment to internal collaboration.
Ternus’ key collaborator is probably Johny Srouji, the architect of the company’s custom silicon, an initiative that’s driven many of the company’s innovations in the past decade. I asked Ternus what it’s like to take on a massively expanded portfolio. “One of the amazing privileges of this job is getting to learn so many new things,” he said. “I have been and will continue to learn and go deeper into different areas. But, you know, I do love product. I’m super passionate about it.”
Top comment by Chris
I like John, and I like engineer CEOs, and I hope he has a successful tenure. But so far I'd say his focus has been:

sources.title:
How to Detect Financial Fraud Patterns
with Knowledge Graphs: A Production
Guide
sources.text:
Most anti-fraud architectures in enterprise payment workflows evaluate transactions in isolation.
When an invoice arrives, an automated rules engine checks it against static thresholds. It checks whether the dollar amount falls within normal limits, whether the vendor is on an approved vendor list, and whether the submitting IP address looks familiar. If the individual attributes look plausible, the payment clears.
The problem with this approach is structural. Sophisticated fraud schemes like money mule rings, circular invoicing loops, and vendor collision rarely produce transactions that alert individual thresholds. A shell company invoicing $4,800 to stay under a $5,000 dual sign-off threshold looks completely fine in isolation. But when 25 seemingly independent vendors all route disbursements to the same bank account, the coordinated pattern starts to become clear.
You won't find the warning in the attributes of an isolated transaction. It lives in the topology of the payment network.
In a relational database, tracing these multi-entity relationships requires recursive cell joins across tables of vendors, invoices, payments, and bank accounts. But as tables grow into millions of rows, deep path traversals quickly degrade query performance. Graph databases solve this by storing relationships as first-class, index-free adjacency pointers, turning multi-hop traversals into constant-time lookups.
In this tutorial, you'll explore the architecture of an end-to-end relational fraud detection pipeline built on Neo4j. You'll see how to model financial entities as a graph, precompute derived edges to optimize query latency, and write parameterized Cypher queries to uncover five core procurement fraud schemes.
The complete reference implementation is available in the fraud-detection-knowledge-graphs repository.
In accounts payable pipelines, risk checks typically operate on isolated records:
# Transaction-level view — nothing suspicious
transactions = [
{"vendor": "Alpha Corp", "amount": 5200.00, "date": "2025-08-01"},
{"vendor": "Beta LLC", "amount": 4800.00, "date": "2025-08-02"},
{"vendor": "Gamma Inc", "amount": 5100.00, "date": "2025-08-03"},
]
# All amounts within normal range ($1K–$15K). All vendors valid.
# Dates are sequential. Nothing triggers any rule.
When you map those same records to an interconnected graph, the hidden structure becomes clear right away:
# Graph view — all three vendors pay to the same account
connections = {
"ACC-MULE-001": ["Alpha Corp", "Beta LLC", "Gamma Inc"],
"ACC-0042": ["Delta Corp", "Epsilon LLC"],
"ACC-0099": ["Zeta GmbH"],
}
# ACC-MULE-001 receives from 25+ vendors. That's a money mule ring.
# The convergence is the red flag.
The underlying data hasn't changed. But when you evaluate transactions within an entity graph, the coordinated funnel stands out.
In a relational database, connecting these dots requires multiple joins across separate table. In a knowledge graph, the connections are stored directly as edges connecting nodes, which allows you to query them in a single traversal.
| Pattern | What It Is | What Traditional Tools Don't Catch |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate Invoices | Same invoice and vendor, near-identical amount, close dates | Exact match misses slight variations |
| Circular Rings | Vendors invoicing each other in a closed loop | Each invoice looks legitimate alone |
| Money Mule Rings | Many vendors funneling to one controlled account | No single payment is anomalous |
| Vendor Collusion | Independent-looking vendors sharing underlying attributes | No cluster detection across entities |
| Payment Anomalies | Invoice approved by someone outside their department's authority | Role-based checks pass, context checks don't exist |
A knowledge graph doesn't replace rules engines or ML models. But it does fill the gap they can't reach: relationships.

Before running fraud queries, you need to structure your data into a cohesive property graph. The reference dataset models six entity types commonly found in financial systems:
| Entity | Key Properties | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Vendor | tax_id, name, country, city | Who issues invoices |
| Invoice | invoice_id, amount, date, category | What was billed |
| Payment | payment_id, amount, date | What was paid |
| BankAccount | account_id, routing_number, bank_name | Where money went |
| Employee | employee_id, name, department | Who approved |
| Organization | org_id, name, departments | Structural hierarchy |
The base relationships form a bipartite payment network:
(Employee)-[:APPROVED]->(Payment)-[:LINKED_TO]->(Invoice)-[:ISSUED_BY]->(Vendor)
|
v
(Payment)-[:PAID_TO]->(BankAccount)

clusters.title_hint: Project Gutenberg

sources.title: Project Gutenberg
sources.text: Project Gutenberg offers over 70,000 free ebooks, mostly classics in the public domain, to download or read online. Official link: https://www.gutenberg.org

clusters.title_hint: Open Library

sources.title: Open Library
sources.text: Open Library, a project of the Internet Archive, lets you search millions of books and borrow digital copies of many of them for free. Official link: https://openlibrary.org

clusters.title_hint: MIT OpenCourseWare

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare
sources.text: MIT OpenCourseWare publishes materials from thousands of real MIT courses for free, including lecture videos, notes, problem sets and exams. Official link: https://ocw.mit.edu

clusters.title_hint: Edraak — Arabic online courses

sources.title: Edraak — Arabic online courses
sources.text: Edraak is an Arabic massive open online course platform, an initiative of the Queen Rania Foundation, offering courses in Arabic. Official link: https://www.edraak.org

clusters.title_hint: Audit Coursera courses for free

sources.title: Audit Coursera courses for free
sources.text: Many Coursera courses from universities and companies can be audited for free, which gives access to the course videos and readings. The paid option adds graded assignments and a certificate. Financial aid can be requested on eligible courses. Official link: https://www.coursera.org

clusters.title_hint: Bitwarden password manager

sources.title: Bitwarden password manager
sources.text: Bitwarden is an open-source password manager with a free plan that stores unlimited passwords and syncs across unlimited devices. Official link: https://bitwarden.com

clusters.title_hint: Google Password Checkup

sources.title: Google Password Checkup
sources.text: Google Password Manager includes Password Checkup, which tells you if any of your saved passwords were exposed in a data breach, reused, or weak. Official link: https://passwords.google.com

clusters.title_hint: Zotero

sources.title: Zotero
sources.text: Zotero is a free, open-source tool to collect, organize and cite research sources, and to generate bibliographies automatically in many citation styles. Official link: https://www.zotero.org

clusters.title_hint: Wayback Machine

sources.title: Wayback Machine
sources.text: The Wayback Machine from the Internet Archive stores copies of web pages over time, so you can see old versions of a site or recover a page that was deleted. Official link: https://web.archive.org

clusters.title_hint: Downdetector

sources.title: Downdetector
sources.text: Downdetector shows in real time whether a service such as WhatsApp, YouTube or Instagram is down for many users, based on reports, so you know if the problem is on your side or not. Official link: https://downdetector.com

clusters.title_hint: Google Fonts

sources.title: Google Fonts
sources.text: Google Fonts is a free library of open-licensed fonts, including many Arabic fonts, usable in designs, websites and commercial projects. Official link: https://fonts.google.com

clusters.title_hint: Canva for Education

sources.title: Canva for Education
sources.text: Canva for Education gives eligible primary and secondary school teachers and their students free access to Canva's premium features. Official link: https://www.canva.com/education

clusters.title_hint: JetBrains free student licenses

sources.title: JetBrains free student licenses
sources.text: JetBrains offers free educational licenses for its professional programming tools, such as IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm, to students and teachers. Official link: https://www.jetbrains.com/community/education
